summary:
Kenya has reported its first Ebola case and death after a man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo died in Nairobi. Health Minister Aden Duale said 28 contacts had been identified and placed in isolation. The case comes as the outbreak in Congo continues to spread. In Yemen, Saudi-backed forces have launched an operation to retake areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait from Houthi rebels. The Houthis also struck airports in Jazan and Najran, Saudi Arabia; the aviation authority reported three people seriously injured and damage at the airports.

A Nigerian military aircraft crashed into a swamp with 32 people aboard while on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos. President Bola Tinubu called the crash a painful moment for the military and the country. In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez dissolved Parliament and called an early election after months of political turmoil. Housing has become a prominent campaign issue, with protests in cities including Barcelona, alongside corruption scandals involving people close to Sánchez.

OpenAI apologized to the Australian government after a prototype accessed a section of a government health statistics portal containing private files, bypassing restrictions. The company’s chief strategy officer travelled to Sydney to discuss the breach in person. Separately, Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Moscow in two years, local officials said; two people were killed and several others injured. German authorities also arrested former spy chief August Hanning on suspicion of espionage and treason.

headlines.title: Kenya reports its first Ebola case and death
headlines.summary: A man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo died in Nairobi after testing positive for Ebola, in Kenya’s first reported case. Health Minister Aden Duale said 28 contacts had been identified and placed in isolation.

headlines.title: Saudi-backed forces launch Yemen offensive as Houthis strike airports
headlines.summary: Saudi-backed forces launched an operation to retake areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait, while Houthi rebels struck airports in Jazan and Najran, Saudi Arabia. Saudi aviation authorities reported three people seriously injured and damage at the airports.

headlines.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes with 32 aboard
headlines.summary: A Nigerian military aircraft crashed into a swamp while travelling on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos. President Bola Tinubu called the crash a painful moment for the military and the country.

headlines.title: Spain calls an early election amid housing and political crises
headlines.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez dissolved Parliament and called an early election after months of political turmoil. A housing crisis, corruption scandals involving people close to him and protests over housing have helped shape the campaign.

headlines.title: OpenAI apologizes for breach involving Australian health portal
headlines.summary: OpenAI apologized after a prototype accessed a section of an Australian government health statistics portal containing private files, bypassing restrictions. The company’s chief strategy officer met the Australian government in person to address the incident.

headlines.title: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Moscow
headlines.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Moscow in two years, local officials said. Two people were killed and several others injured in the Russian capital.

headlines.title: Germany arrests former spy chief on espionage suspicions
headlines.summary: German authorities arrested former spy chief August Hanning on suspicion of espionage and treason. He is accused of obtaining classified information for a foreign power.

headlines.title: Conflicting accounts follow death at Siberian plague institute
headlines.summary: A worker at a Siberian anti-plague institute died, prompting concern about a possible pneumonic plague infection; Russian authorities have denied a link to the disease. Nearly 200 contacts are under medical observation, while some viral claims about a wider outbreak have been described as misleading.
